content:
The Inequalities chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Inequalities tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Inequalities

Linear, quadratic, rational and modulus inequalities, integer-solution counts and the AM–GM inequality for max/min.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Multiplying by a negative reverses the inequality.
  • (x−a)(x−b) < 0 ⇒ a < x < b (a<b).
  • |x| < a ⇒ −a < x < a; |x| > a ⇒ x < −a or x > a.
  • For x>0, x + k/x has minimum 2√k at x = √k.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Forgetting to flip the sign when multiplying/dividing by a negative.
  • Including the point where a rational expression is undefined.
  • Mishandling squared factors like (x−1)².
